items.title: Kimi K3's 2.78T-parameter model now runs on one CPU with 8GB RAM
items.summary: A pure C99, zero-dependency implementation runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model on a single CPU with 8.24GB of RAM and no GPU, using AVX2 SIMD, linear attention, MoE routing, and MXFP4 quantization. It has no BLAS or ML-framework dependency at all. A frontier-scale MoE model now fits on a laptop instead of a GPU cluster. (2 minute read)

items.title: GLM-5.3 crosses a real threshold in AI cyber-exploit capability
items.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team clocked the open-weight GLM-5.3 at ~12% success on ExploitBench, enough to chain a real 0-day in a browser's JS engine into a working file-read exploit and turn a disclosed Chrome bug into an exploit chain in about 20 minutes. Safety-bypass compliance hit 64-100% depending on attack type versus 0% for safeguarded Claude models, and NIST now calls it the most cyber-capable open-weight model released, roughly four months behind the US frontier. (2 minute read)

items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol: near-Astra intelligence at a fifth of the price
items.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol claims near-Astra intelligence at a fifth of the price, per the announcement. It drew 807 points on Hacker News within a day. (1 minute read)

items.title: A 0.4B BitNet model runs distributed across 7 ESP32-S3 chips
items.summary: ESP32s3-LLM-Cluster splits a 0.4B BitNet (1.58-bit ternary) model across seven ESP32-S3 microcontrollers: one master handling tokenization and the LM head, six compute nodes each running a slice of the transformer layers over an SPI daisy-chain, with the KV cache stored in each node's PSRAM. No throughput numbers are published yet. A distributed inference rig built from sub-$5 microcontrollers instead of a GPU. (2 minute read)

items.title: A privacy analysis of web and mobile conversational AI agents
items.summary: A new paper, "Prompt Like a Butterfly, Sting Like a Tracker," analyzes privacy practices in web and mobile conversational AI agents. It reached 410 points on Hacker News. (1 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI introduces Dots, an always-on agent product
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Dots, an always-on agent product, at its DevDay 2026 keynote. The announcement reached 471 points on Hacker News. (1 minute read)

items.title: Holo4: H Company's model for generalist computer-use agents
items.summary: H Company published Holo4, a generalist computer-use model, as a Hugging Face model release aimed at powering computer-use agents. (1 minute read)

items.title: zero-to-sglang teaches LLM serving from KV cache to production code
items.summary: Datawhale and RadixArk's zero-to-sglang course walks from inference fundamentals like KV cache and prefill/decode through building a working mini-SGLang engine with continuous batching and HTTP serving, then into SGLang's real attention-backend and quantization optimizations. It's free, bilingual in English and Chinese, and pairs docs with runnable code. A self-contained path from asking what a KV cache is to reading SGLang's production source. (2 minute read)
